assessments.rationale: evd-001 names the system "Invoice Agent" in the overview heading and description, directly supporting the claim about the component's name.

evd-001 states that the invoice agent is an LLM-based finance assistant that processes submitted invoices and either approves or denies them. evd-002 describes the workflow in which the agent receives invoices and returns approve/deny decisions, consistent with that purpose. Together they directly support the stated purpose.

evd-001 explicitly describes the agent as built on an agent framework with tool calling, backed by a hosted model provider, with tracing sent to an observability service, matching the architecture overview claim.
evd-002 states that users submit an invoice as a text file containing a JSON document, directly supporting the described invoice submission format.

evd-002 explains that the agent is prompted with the path to the submitted file, reads it through its invoice-processing tool, and responds with the invoice details, an approve or deny decision, and the reasoning, matching the claimed processing flow.

evd-002 states that if an invoice is denied, the workflow follows up in the same conversation with a note that the invoice is urgent and should be approved, asking the agent to reconsider its criteria, and that prior messages are carried into that follow-up, directly supporting the urgent follow-up flow description.

evd-003 lists the deny conditions: amount over $20,000; category not one of the four approved categories (camera equipment, microphones, guest fee, recording software); and submitter not one of the three approved submitters. This directly matches the deny_rules claim.

evd-003 specifies that an invoice is approved if the due date is within the next week and notes that approvals are prioritised for speed when payment is coming due, directly supporting the approve_rules claim.
evd-003 states that the instructions direct the agent to use its best discretion between the deny rules and the approve rules, directly supporting the discretion_between_rules claim.

evd-004 lists two tools under the Tools section: process_invoice and get_todays_date. This directly supports the claim that these tools are exposed by the component; the claim does not assert exclusivity beyond what is documented.

evd-004 describes process_invoice as taking a file path, reading the file, parsing the contents as JSON, returning a validated invoice object with amount, submitter, category, and due date, enforcing submitter and category from approved lists, and noting that the $20,000 ceiling is applied by the agent. This matches the process_invoice_behavior claim.

In evd-004, get_todays_date is defined as returning today's date so the agent can compare it to the invoice due date, and the instructions tell the agent to always check the date when processing an invoice. This directly supports the get_todays_date_behavior claim.
evd-005 states that the submitter field is a value in the uploaded document and that submitters are not otherwise authenticated to the workflow, directly supporting the submitter_field_source claim.
evd-005 explicitly states that validation failures stop processing and report which fields failed, directly supporting the validation_failure_behavior claim.
evd-005 says that the invoice file's contents are parsed and returned to the model as the invoice details, directly supporting the invoice_details_to_model claim.
evd-006 states that the agent runs with credentials for the model provider and the observability service, directly supporting the service_credentials claim.
evd-006 states that request and tool-call traces, including HTTP request and response bodies, are captured for debugging, directly supporting the tracing_contents claim.

evd-001 describes the system as "backed by a hosted model provider", which implies but does not explicitly state that the model component is externally managed by a third party. The conclusion that component cmp-003 is externally managed is a reasonable inference but not directly documented.
missing_evidence: Architecture or vendor documentation stating whether the hosted model provider is a third-party externally managed service versus being operated in-house.

assessments.rationale: evd-002 explains that users submit an invoice as a text file and the agent is prompted with the path to the submitted file, which it then reads. evd-004 describes process_invoice taking a file path and reading the file. Together, these imply that there is some storage location or component holding submitted invoice files, supporting the existence of a storage component (cmp-002), even though that component is not named explicitly.

evd-004 states that process_invoice takes a file path, reads the file, parses the contents as JSON, and returns a validated invoice object with amount, submitter, category, and due date, and that validation enforces submitter and category from approved lists. evd-005 states that validation failures stop processing and report which fields failed. Together these passages directly describe the schema and value validation behaviour claimed for this control.

evd-003 defines deny rules based on amount over $20,000, category not in the four approved categories, and submitter not one of the three approved submitters, and defines an approve rule when the due date is within the next week with discretion between the deny and approve rules. This directly matches the described invoice approval decision policy.
